CweFindings.Description: The code uses deprecated or obsolete functions, which suggests that the code has not been actively reviewed or maintained.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Obsolete Function
CweFindings.Explanation: BinaryFormatter is used for serialization and deserialization. BinaryFormatter is obsolete in modern .NET and is no longer a supported serialization mechanism.

CweFindings.Description: When converting from one data type to another, such as long to integer, data can be omitted or translated in a way that produces unexpected values. If the resulting values are used in a sensitive context, then dangerous behaviors may occur.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types
CweFindings.Explanation: GetSequenceIdFromSelectedDBSequence receives an Int64 sequence value and casts it directly to int. Values outside the Int32 range are truncated/wrapped, producing an incorrect sequence identifier.

CweFindings.Description: The product performs a calculation that generates incorrect or unintended results that are later used in security-critical decisions or resource management.
CweFindings.Name: Incorrect Calculation
CweFindings.Explanation: GetCatalogItemsPaginated computes pageSize * pageIndex using unchecked Int32 arithmetic for Skip. Large request values can overflow and produce an incorrect pagination offset.

CweFindings.Description: The product allocates memory based on an untrusted, large size value, but it does not ensure that the size is within expected limits, allowing arbitrary amounts of memory to be allocated.
CweFindings.Name: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value
CweFindings.Explanation: The pageSize query parameter is accepted without an upper bound and passed to Take(pageSize).ToList(), allowing a client to request materialization of an arbitrarily large page from the catalog.

CweFindings.Description: The product uses the singleton pattern when creating a resource within a multithreaded environment.
CweFindings.Name: Use of Singleton Pattern Without Synchronization in a Multithreaded Context
CweFindings.Explanation: When UseMockData is enabled, ApplicationModule registers CatalogServiceMock as a SingleInstance. Its shared mutable catalogItems list is accessed by request methods and modified by CreateCatalogItem, UpdateCatalogItem, and RemoveCatalogItem without synchronization, allowing concurrent collection reads and writes.

CweFindings.Description: The product does not properly synchronize shared data, such as static variables across threads, which can lead to undefined behavior and unpredictable data changes.

CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes multiple threads or processes to allow temporary access to a shared resource that can only be exclusive to one process at a time, but it does not properly synchronize these actions, which might cause simultaneous accesses of this resource by multiple threads or processes.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Synchronization

CweFindings.Description: The product utilizes a shared resource in a concurrent manner but does not attempt to synchronize access to the resource.

CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that is intended to identify a file or directory that is located underneath a restricted parent directory, but the product does not properly neutralize special elements within the pathname that can cause the pathname to resolve to a location that is outside of the restricted directory.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
CweFindings.Explanation: The MVC create and edit actions bind PictureFileName from request model data. PicController.Index uses that stored value in Path.Combine and reads the resulting path with File.ReadAllBytes without verifying that the resolved path remains under the pictures directory. A crafted filename containing traversal segments can escape the intended directory. The ported controller combines the filename with an empty webRoot, leaving the read unconstrained.

CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize sequences such as .. that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Name: Relative Path Traversal
CweFindings.Explanation: PictureFileName is request-bindable through catalog create and edit. PicController.Index passes it to Path.Combine and reads the result without canonicalizing or checking the parent directory, so relative segments such as .. can escape the intended picture directory.

CweFindings.Description: The product uses external input to construct a pathname that should be within a restricted directory, but it does not properly neutralize absolute path sequences such as /abs/path that can resolve to a location that is outside of that directory.
CweFindings.Name: Absolute Path Traversal
CweFindings.Explanation: PictureFileName is request-bindable through catalog create and edit. An absolute filename supplied to Path.Combine can replace the intended base directory; the resulting path is passed to File.ReadAllBytes without a containment check.

CweFindings.Description: The product receives input from an upstream component, but it does not restrict or incorrectly restricts the input before it is used as an identifier for a resource that may be outside the intended sphere of control.
CweFindings.Name: Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection')
CweFindings.Explanation: Catalog create and edit request models bind PictureFileName. PicController.Index uses this value as the file resource identifier passed to Path.Combine and File.ReadAllBytes without restricting it to an approved filename. This overlaps the path traversal already documented under CWE-22/23/36.

CweFindings.Description: The product deserializes untrusted data without sufficiently ensuring that the resulting data will be valid.
CweFindings.Name: Deserialization of Untrusted Data
CweFindings.Explanation: Serializing.DeserializeBinary is a public method that passes its Stream directly to BinaryFormatter.Deserialize without validating the stream contents. No call site for DeserializeBinary was found in the target solution, so externally reachable exploitability is not established by this scan.

CveFindings.Description: [CVE-2026-40021](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4f7c-pmjv-c25w): Apache log4net versions before 3.3.0 do not sanitize XML 1.0 forbidden characters in MDC properties and identity, which can cause affected log events to be silently dropped.
